entities.summary:
Colaeus (b. 700 BCE, Samos) was a criminal or outlaw of the Classical era, active in Samos. Known in the fields of explorers & navigators.

As a notorious figure of the ancient world, Colaeus's exploits have been passed down through the ages, with some accounts suggesting he was a skilled navigator who charted the Aegean Sea. His most notable achievement was the navigation of the Isthmus of Corinth, a feat that earned him a place in the annals of ancient Greek history.

Despite his notoriety, Colaeus's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by the more famous figures of the time, such as Socrates and Alexander the Great. However, his contributions to the field of navigation and exploration remain significant, and his name continues to be mentioned in academic circles today.

In the words of the ancient Greek historian Herodotus, 'Colaeus was a man of great cunning and intelligence, who navigated the waters of the Aegean with ease, and was feared by all who crossed his path.'
